static_traits.name: Lin Yisen
static_traits.social_status: Tense relationship with parents due to home-buying worries; having a few friends to confide in, but has not yet discussed this problem with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy received in the past; no similar psychological problems in the past
static_traits.language_features: Neutral attitude, clear expression, willing to cooperate in discussion, able to describe specific trigger situations and their impact

basic_info.main_problem: I believe I can never buy a house of my own, because I work as a restaurant server and still live with my parents. This belief causes me pain and despair.
basic_info.core_demands: The persistent thought of 'never affording a house' has begun affecting my mental health and overall well-being, so I hope counseling will ease and improve it.
growth_experiences: After starting work as a restaurant server three years ago, the thought 'I will never afford a house' gradually appeared; these thoughts are more frequent after work and when browsing listings.

Seeing peers or people around achieve home ownership gradually reinforced the 'cannot afford a house' belief; during this time budgeting and saving were tried, but still considered insufficient to change reality.

core_beliefs: I can never buy my own house

special_situations.event: After getting off work at the restaurant
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my income is only a server's wage, I can never save enough money to buy a house
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying budgeting and saving to counter unease
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never afford a house

special_situations.event: Browsing property listings and prices online
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If house prices keep rising, my efforts are also meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuing strict budgeting and saving, but mentally negating their effect
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: House prices are getting higher and higher; I am destined to never afford one

special_situations.event: Seeing peers buy houses or share house-buying news on social media
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not bought a house like my peers, it shows I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding discussing this problem with friends, bearing the anxiety alone
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot buy a house like them

special_situations.event: Being reminded of reality when returning to the home environment of living with parents
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I still live with my parents, it means I am not independent enough; buying a house is impossible for me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to 'prove' that I am working hard by saving money harder and demanding more of myself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not independent enough; buying a house is impossible for me

core_conflict.wish: Longs for financial independence and a home of her own
core_conflict.fear: Fear of never achieving the goal, of being proven a failure by reality and peers' achievements
defense_goal: Using pessimistic anticipation and rationalized interpretation to reduce the disappointment and anxiety that hope brings

object_relations.self_representation: An economically disadvantaged self, not yet independent
object_relations.object_representation: Judgmental and more successful 'others' (such as peers, social standards)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites them to explore more flexible possibilities or propose feasible 'small steps'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to interpret the counselor's exploration as dismissing real difficulties, reinforcing the belief that 'reality is just limited income and high house prices'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Repeating the objective limitations of the market and income in a calm, fact-stating tone, emphasizing 'this is reality', and reducing emotional expression.

manifestations: Repeatedly experiencing the despair of 'never affording a house'
Believing the goal is impossible to achieve, feeling 'trapped'
Hard to focus on activities once enjoyed (soccer, reading)

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Stating in absolutist terms: 'never affording a house'
Treating 'high house prices / low server wages' as unchangeable truth
Emphasizing 'this is just reality', hard to accept other possibilities

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: Not discussing this problem with friends, choosing to digest the anxiety alone
Feels tense at home due to worry, but rarely expresses specific needs or seeks support

positive_force: Having financial management and self-management awareness (have tried budgeting and saving)
Work relatively stable (has worked as a restaurant server for three years)
Has some social support (a few friends to confide in)
negative_force: Marked catastrophizing and 'black-and-white' thinking, interpreting the future in terms of 'never/impossible'
Mental filtering: over-focuses on rising house prices and limited income, ignoring potential possibilities
Predicting the future: asserting the inability to buy a house without evidence, triggering hopelessness
Comparison and despair: comparing home buying with peers, reinforcing self-denial

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent worry and catastrophic automatic thoughts around the house-buying problem
antecedent: After getting off work at the restaurant
Seeing news of peers buying homes
Returning to the home environment of living with parents
target_behavior.core_reason: Integrating limited server income and rising house prices into the belief of 'never being able to buy a house', forming catastrophizing and black-and-white cognition
target_behavior.function: Avoiding uncertainty and potential failure, lowering expectations and disappointment through pessimistic anticipation
target_behavior.consequence: Decline in work performance, difficulty focusing on leisure activities like soccer or reading, relationship tension with parents, low mood and hopelessness
